name: ME-01
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+11 district with strong fundamentals baseline (~21-point margin)
Incumbent Chellie Pingree running for re-election with large cash advantage ($423K vs $20K)
No outside spending against her and Polymarket prices her at 96%
model.rationale: The baseline model's D+20.8 margin aligns with the district's D+11 lean plus incumbency and a favorable environment, and no evidence contradicts it. Pingree's overwhelming financial edge and 96% market pricing confirm Safe D status.
model.watch: A major late-cycle national wave toward Republicans or unexpected candidate developments could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Maine's 1st District leans Democratic by about 11 points on the partisan baseline, and incumbent Chellie Pingree is seeking re-election with the advantages that come with incumbency. The quantitative model combines district lean, a favorable national environment, incumbency, and a modest money edge into an expected margin of roughly 21 points.

There are no public general-election polls or expert ratings for this race, so the forecast rests on fundamentals. Pingree has a large financial advantage over Republican Ronald Russell, with no outside spending opposing her, and prediction markets price her win probability at about 96 percent. All available evidence points to a safe Democratic hold.
